original_text: Meiosis I¨Prophase I:¤DNA tightly coils into chromosomes¤Spindle fibers appear                                                                     ¤Nucleolus & nuclear membrane disassemble/disappear¨Same as in mitosis!
explanation: Prophase I is the initial stage of Meiosis I. During this phase, several key structural changes occur that are identical to the events in mitotic prophase: the chromatin DNA tightly condenses and coils to form visible chromosomes, spindle fibers begin to appear from the centrosomes, and both the nucleolus and the nuclear membrane disassemble and disappear.

questions.q: Which of the following events occur during Prophase I of meiosis that are identical to mitosis?
opts: Pairing of homologous chromosomes to form tetrads.
DNA tightly coiling into chromosomes, appearance of spindle fibers, and disassembly of the nucleolus and nuclear membrane.
Separation of sister chromatids to opposite poles.
Replication of genomic DNA in the cytoplasm.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because the slide states: 'DNA tightly coils into chromosomes', 'Spindle fibers appear', and 'Nucleolus & nuclear membrane disassemble/disappear', noting these are 'Same as in mitosis!'
